proposed_widenings.name: container_storage_and_retrieval
proposed_widenings.justification: The item's primary mechanic is a persistent extradimensional container with its own contents, capacity limits, retrieval procedure, and failure modes. Existing magic-item families only model passive grants, activations, reactions, summons, or composites of those; none represent a durable item-owned storage space or actions that move objects into and out of that space.
proposed_widenings.evidence: "The bag can hold up to 500 pounds, not exceeding a volume of 64 cubic feet." and "Retrieving an item from the bag requires a Utilize action."

proposed_widenings.name: container_failure_and_contents_disposition
proposed_widenings.justification: The bag has deterministic state transitions tied to overload, damage, inversion, and breathable air for creatures inside. Those are not expressible as current effect atoms on creatures, nor as existing item destruction policies, because they depend on tracked container contents and interior occupancy.
proposed_widenings.evidence: "If the bag is overloaded, pierced, or torn, it is destroyed, and its contents are scattered in the Astral Plane." and "If the bag is turned inside out, its contents spill forth unharmed, but the bag must be put right before it can be used again." and "The bag holds enough air for 10 minutes of breathing, divided by the number of breathing creatures inside."

proposed_widenings.name: cross_item_extradimensional_breach
proposed_widenings.justification: Placing the bag inside another extradimensional space causes both items to be destroyed, creates a one-shot gate at a location, and forces nearby creatures through it to the Astral Plane. This is a cross-item interaction plus a transient area hazard, not a normal activation, passive grant, or reaction.
proposed_widenings.evidence: "Placing a Bag of Holding inside an extradimensional space created by a Handy Haversack, Portable Hole, or similar item instantly destroys both items and opens a gate to the Astral Plane." and "Any creature within a 10-foot-radius Sphere centered on the gate is sucked through it to a random location on the Astral Plane."

notes: No content file was authored. The random Astral destination is DM-owned, but the blocking issue is earlier: the current surface has no honest family for stateful container items or for item-to-item extradimensional breach mechanics.
